nodes.content: Build a dependency-upgrade analyzer that distinguishes client-reachable behavioral incompatibilities from harmless upstream changes despite dynamic dispatch and incomplete code.
requirements: Achieve at least 90% recall and 90% precision on 100 labeled upgrade scenarios.
Provide reproducible client-level witnesses for incompatibilities; explicitly identify uncertainty caused by unavailable code or reflection.

nodes.content: Combine client-seeded points-to reachability with differential execution to filter harmless changes, replay incompatibilities, and flag reflection or missing code.
How should client-seeded reachability handle reflective calls and missing library bodies without falsely dismissing reachable regressions?
Constant-string reflection resolution plus unknown labels for unresolved targets and missing bodies should reduce false-safe classifications versus closed-world reachability.
Implement constant-string reflection resolution, propagate unknowns through missing bodies, replay differential witnesses, and compare false-safe rates against closed-world reachability.
Implement ReflectionResolver for constant-string Class.forName/getMethod calls and propagate UNKNOWN through missing library bodies in client-seeded call graphs.
ReflectionResolver emits client-seeded call graphs with resolved constant-string targets and UNKNOWN edges for unresolved reflection or absent bodies.
Run UpgradeBench-100 against ReflectionResolver and closed-world reachability, measuring false-safe rates and UNKNOWN coverage for reflective and missing-body cases.
On UpgradeBench-100, false-safe errors fell from 8 to 1; UNKNOWN labeling covered 17 of 19 unresolved cases.
Run ReflectionResolver on ReflectionStress-20 with computed method names and omitted bodies; compare false-safe rates against closed-world reachability.
On ReflectionStress-20, both approaches made 4 false-safe classifications: computed-name callbacks from omitted wrappers escaped UNKNOWN propagation.
Can boundary summaries capture computed-name callbacks from omitted wrappers without marking every downstream client call UNKNOWN?
Symbolic callback-and-name summaries for omitted wrappers should reduce ReflectionStress-20 false-safe errors below 4 without labeling all 20 UNKNOWN.
Add wrapper-boundary summaries for callback arguments and symbolic names; rerun ReflectionStress-20, tracking false-safe errors and UNKNOWN labels.
Implement symbolic wrapper-boundary callback summaries in ReflectionResolver and rerun ReflectionStress-20, counting false-safe classifications and UNKNOWN labels.
On ReflectionStress-20, false-safe errors remained 4; summaries missed callbacks stored in omitted wrappers' fields.
Extend ReflectionResolver with field-sensitive summaries for callbacks stored by omitted wrappers; rerun ReflectionStress-20 measuring false-safe errors and UNKNOWN labels.
Field-sensitive summaries reduced ReflectionStress-20 false-safe errors from 4 to 1, with 7 of 20 scenarios labeled UNKNOWN.
Which client-to-callback path causes ReflectionStress-20’s remaining false-safe error despite field-sensitive summaries?
The remaining false-safe path likely passes through an omitted wrapper’s callback container alias, requiring alias-aware field summaries.
Trace the remaining client-to-callback path, add alias-aware field summaries if confirmed, and rerun ReflectionStress-20 for false-safe errors.
Trace ReflectionStress-20’s residual callback path in ReflectionResolver, implement alias-aware field summaries, and recount false-safe errors and UNKNOWN labels.
Trace confirmed a container alias; alias-aware summaries cut ReflectionStress-20 false-safe errors from 1 to 0, with 8 UNKNOWN labels.
Ablate alias propagation in ReflectionResolver on the residual scenario; compare callback paths and false-safe classifications with alias-aware summaries.
Without alias propagation, ReflectionStress-20 still had zero false-safe errors; UNKNOWN rose from 8 to 12, contradicting alias necessity.
Replay ReflectionStress-20’s residual case with UNKNOWN fallback temporarily disabled, comparing concrete callback paths with and without alias propagation.
With UNKNOWN fallback disabled, alias propagation recovered the residual callback path; without it, the case became false-safe.
Retain alias-aware summaries for concrete callback paths and UNKNOWN fallback for unresolved ones; both prevent different kinds of missed regressions.
Synthesize minimized, version-pinned client tests for reachable changes, comparing observable outcomes while reporting untestable paths as uncertain.
How can generated client tests reproduce changed behavior across both versions without treating nondeterministic output or missing code as incompatibility?
Generate minimized client harnesses, pin versions and seeds, replay five times, normalize observables, and mark missing-code paths uncertain.
Implement WitnessHarness for minimized client calls, pinned versions and seeds, five replays, normalized observables, and missing-code uncertainty.
WitnessHarness exports minimized client tests with locked dependency coordinates, five-run outcome traces, normalized diffs, and explicit missing-code uncertainty.
Run WitnessHarness on UpgradeBench-100, measuring client-witness reproducibility, harmless-change false positives, and missing-code uncertainty against labels.
On UpgradeBench-100, only 18/25 incompatibilities yielded stable five-run witnesses; six harmless cases triggered clock-dependent false positives.
Defer incompatibility verdicts from unstable traces and replace clock normalization with deterministic clock injection before reassessing witness coverage.
Add deterministic environment injection and three-way verdicts: witnessed incompatibility, verified harmless change, or uncertainty with explicit causes.
Which environment controls eliminate clock-driven false positives without hiding genuine timing-sensitive client incompatibilities?
Injecting identical virtual clocks while comparing version-specific call sequences should remove six clock false positives yet preserve timing-order regressions.
Inject matched virtual clocks into WitnessHarness and compare five-run traces and timing-order labels across UpgradeBench-100.
On UpgradeBench-100, virtual clocks eliminated all six clock-driven false positives and retained all three labeled timing-order regressions.
Stress-test virtual clocks on ClockShift-12 with matched randomized tick schedules, checking labeled timeout regressions and harmless jitter.
On ClockShift-12, matched randomized ticks masked 2 of 5 timing-order regressions by synchronizing callbacks across versions.
Can shared wall-clock inputs coexist with independent callback schedulers so timing regressions remain visible without restoring clock-driven false positives?
Shared injected wall-clock reads with independent event-loop scheduling should recover both masked ClockShift-12 regressions without clock false positives.
Separate wall-clock injection from callback scheduling; rerun ClockShift-12 and UpgradeBench-100, checking recovered regressions and clock false positives.
Modify WitnessHarness to share wall-clock reads but schedule callbacks independently; rerun ClockShift-12 and UpgradeBench-100 for timing recall and false positives.
Independent scheduling recovered all 5 ClockShift-12 timing regressions; UpgradeBench-100 retained zero clock-driven false positives.
Adopt shared virtual wall-clock reads with independent callback schedulers; synchronized ticks concealed regressions despite removing spurious clock differences.
Introduce VerdictGate to combine reachability, reproducible differential witnesses, and explicit UNKNOWN labels; measure verdict precision and recall on UpgradeBench-100.
What VerdictGate criteria distinguish verified harmless changes from UNKNOWN paths when no differential witness reproduces?
Require closed client reachability and matched stable traces for harmless verdicts; classify unresolved edges or unstable replays UNKNOWN.
Implement VerdictGate using ReflectionResolver closure and WitnessHarness five-run traces; emit UNKNOWN for unresolved edges, missing bodies, or unstable replays.
VerdictGate emits witnessed incompatibility, verified harmless, or UNKNOWN, attaching minimized replay traces and unresolved-reflection or missing-code reasons.
Evaluate VerdictGate on UpgradeBench-100, reporting incompatibility precision, recall, reproducible witness coverage, and UNKNOWN counts.
On UpgradeBench-100, VerdictGate achieved 92% recall (23/25), 95.8% precision (23/24), 23 reproducible witnesses, and 10 UNKNOWN verdicts.
Run VerdictGate on held-out BoundaryBench-30 with computed reflection and unavailable bodies; measure false-safe harmless verdicts and cause-labeled UNKNOWN coverage.
BoundaryBench-30 yielded zero false-safe harmless verdicts; all 9 incomplete-code cases carried explicit UNKNOWN causes.
Can observed client callback traces resolve any of BoundaryBench-30’s nine incomplete-code UNKNOWN verdicts without assuming behavior for unavailable code?
Recording callback targets during pinned client replays should resolve at least three of nine UNKNOWN cases without increasing false-safe verdicts.
Instrument callback entry points in pinned replays, add observed edges to reachability, then reassess nine UNKNOWN cases and false-safe counts.
Instrument WitnessHarness callback entries, merge observed targets into VerdictGate, and rerun BoundaryBench-30 to count resolved UNKNOWNs and false-safe verdicts.
BoundaryBench-30 resolved 3/9 UNKNOWNs with zero false-safe verdicts, but a nondeterministic callback caused one false incompatibility (80% precision).
Run ten independent matched-seed BoundaryBench-30 replays through VerdictGate, measuring callback stability, false incompatibilities, and resolved UNKNOWNs.
Across ten BoundaryBench-30 seeds, the callback mismatch vanished under four seeds; VerdictGate still issued one false incompatibility.
Retain conservative UNKNOWN verdicts for seed-unstable callbacks; accept observed-edge incompatibilities only with stable cross-seed client witnesses.
